subject: Whistic API key rotation + request for SOC2 evidence sample extract
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Chen <bryan.chen@everledger.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Whistic API key rotation + request for SOC2 evidence sample extract

Hi Bryan —

Hope you’re well. We’re preparing the SOC 2 readiness packet for EverLedger and want to pull a small sample of the evidence currently hosted in your Whistic profile to validate ingestion and mapping on our side. Two asks: 

1) Could you provision a short‑lived, scoped Whistic API key (read‑only, profile X: evidence metadata + attachments) that we can use to pull a sample export (no more than ~50 artifacts)? If possible set TTL to 7 days.

2) If you prefer not to issue an API key, could you export and drop a tarball of the sample artifacts into the S3 path below with a manifest.csv of filenames and CAIQ mapping? Our S3 bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/everledger/soc2-samples/ (we will provide a presigned upload URL if needed).

Jordan and Kimberly here will handle the ingest and CAIQ -> internal mapping. We just need the minimal evidence set that demonstrates control coverage for encryption (KMS), access logs, and sample SOC2 artifacts (policy PDFs, key rotation screenshot exports, syslog snippet).

Security note: the key should be scoped to the profile id only and not include administrative read/write. Please confirm the scope and TTL.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround, ideally within 24–48 hours since this is blocking a runbook dry‑run on Tuesday.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: requested_sample_manifest.csv (placeholder for items we will accept)
From: Bryan Chen <bryan.chen@everledger.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Whistic API key rotation + request for SOC2 evidence sample extract

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can do a scoped readonly API key for the profile and set a 7‑day TTL. I will have our platform team generate a key that only returns evidence metadata and attachment download URLs for the profile id you referenced. We won’t include any admin endpoints.

Two logistical notes: 
- We will redact user PII in the attachments (we'll remove personal email addresses from screenshots) — ok?
- For large attachments we’ll provide presigned S3 URLs; small docs we’ll attach directly.

I’ll have the key created and share it as a secure note; alternatively I can upload the sample bundle to your S3 path if you share a presigned PUT. Which do you prefer?

Regards,
Bryan Chen
Head of Security Operations, EverLedger
bryan.chen@everledger.com

Subject: Re: Whistic API key rotation + request for SOC2 evidence sample extract

Thanks Bryan —

Presigned PUT to our S3 path is easiest for us (we’ll accept a single tar.gz and the manifest.csv). If you can provide the key instead we will request that your team rotate it immediately after the pull. Either approach works.

A couple of specifics for the manifest.csv to make mapping simpler: columns: filename, whistic_artifact_id, control_tag (SIG/CAIQ mapping), artifact_type (pdf/screenshot/log), last_modified. If you can include sample JSON metadata for one artifact that shows your metadata schema, that will speed ingestion.

Jordan: can you prepare the presigned PUT and share it back to Bryan?

Kimberly: can you make sure our CAIQ mapping template is attached (I attached requested_sample_manifest.csv earlier) so they can mirror it?

Appreciate it — if you can get the bundle uploaded by EOD tomorrow that keeps us on schedule.

—Michael

> On May 23, 2026, at 11:04 AM, Bryan Chen <bryan.chen@everledger.com> wrote:

Subject: Re: Whistic API key rotation + request for SOC2 evidence sample extract

All —

We uploaded the sample bundle to the presigned path you provided. Files: everledger_soc2_sample_20260523.tar.gz (contains 42 artifacts) and requested_sample_manifest.csv (attached). Also created a scoped API key and put it in a secure note; to be safe I’ve attached a one‑time text file with the token name (we will not email the token itself). Token name: EL_WHST_READ_20260523.

Notes for your team: 
- We redacted user emails in screenshots and removed unique identifiers from logs where feasible.
- The manifest contains a control_tag column that maps to our internal SIG/CAIQ crosswalk — we included sample mappings for encryption, key rotation, and audit logging.
- We will rotate the scoped key in 7 days automatically. If you need extended access please request via security@everledger.com.

Attachment stubs: whistic_api_key_scoped_readonly.txt (token name only), requested_sample_manifest.csv

If anything in the package looks off (wrong artifact types, missing timestamps), tell me and we’ll re-export.

Thanks — Bryan
